Administration territoriale : le MATD lance un appel à candidatures pour recruter préfets et gouverneurs
items.description: La ministère de l’Administration du Territoire et de la Décentralisation (MATD), Djénabou Touré, à lancé un appel à candidatures interne en vue de sélectionner des fonctionnaires appelés à exercer les fonctions de préfet et de gouverneur de région. Dans un document en date du lundi 14 septembre, le département de l’Administration du Territoire et de la Décentralisation explique que cette initiative s’inscrit dans une dynamique de renforcement de l’administration territoriale et de valorisation du mérite, de l’expérience et des compétences des cadres de l’État. L’objectif affiché est également d’améliorer la qualité des responsables chargés d’exercer les fonctions d’autorité territoriale, ainsi que la coordination et la mise en œuvre des politiques publiques sur l’ensemble du territoire national. Gouverneurs : représenter et coordonner l’action de l’État Selon le MATD, le gouverneur de région aura notamment pour mission de représenter l’État au niveau régional, d’assurer la coordination et la supervision de l’action des services déconcentrés et de conduire les arbitrages interservices sur les questions relevant de la compétence de l’État. Il devra également contribuer à la prévention et à la gestion des crises et situations sensibles, au développement économique et social de la région, ainsi qu’à la mise en œuvre des orientations et décisions de l’administration centrale. Les préfets, relais de l’État dans les préfectures Pour la fonction de préfet, le ministère recherche des cadres capables de représenter l’État au niveau préfectoral et d’assurer la coordination de l’action des services déconcentrés. Cinq ans d’expérience au minimum L’appel à candidatures fixe plusieurs conditions aux postulants. Ceux-ci doivent notamment être en situation administrative régulière, être disponibles et aptes à la mobilité géographique et accepter de servir sur toute l’étendue du territoire national. Ils doivent également s’engager à respecter les principes de neutralité, de loyauté, de réserve, d’impartialité, d’intégrité et de continuité du service public. Sur le plan des qualifications, les candidats doivent notamment être titulaires d’un diplôme en sciences sociales, administration publique, administration territoriale ou dans un domaine équivalent et justifier d’au moins cinq ans d’expérience professionnelle dans le domaine de l’Administration du Territoire. Le MATD exige également des aptitudes en communication institutionnelle et en représentation de l’État, ainsi qu’une capacité à prévenir et gérer les conflits et les situations de crise. Une bonne connaissance des réalités économiques, sociales, culturelles et sécuritaires des territoires, ainsi qu’une capacité à travailler avec les différents acteurs territoriaux, figurent également parmi les compétences recherchées. Les dossiers à déposer avant le 27 septembre Les fonctionnaires intéressés doivent fournir notamment une copie de leur acte d’engagement à la Fonction publique, une lettre de motivation adressée à la ministre de l’Administration du Territoire et de la Décentralisation, un curriculum vitae détaillé, les copies certifiées conformes des diplômes et attestations de formation, une copie de leur pièce d’identité ainsi que tout document justifiant leur expérience professionnelle et leurs atouts. La date limite de dépôt est fixée au 27 septembre 2026 à 23h59. Le ministère rappelle enfin que toute fausse déclaration ou production de document falsifié entraînera les sanctions prévues par les textes en vigueur. items.description: Tottenham Hotspur head coach Roberto De Zerbi has raised doubts over Mohammed Kudus’ availability for Ghana’s upcoming 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers, admitting the midfielder is still some way from full fitness. The Ghana international returned to action late last month for the first time since suffering an injury in January 2026, coming on as a substitute against Newcastle United. Speaking ahead of Tottenham’s Carabao Cup fixture against Liverpool, De Zerbi highlighted Kudus, Mateus Fernandez and Connor Gallagher among the players still working their way back to full fitness. “Mat Fernandez, Connor Gallagher and Kudus are not in the best condition yet.” De Zerbi also explained that Kudus can operate as a number 10 and provide a more attacking option for Tottenham. “Kudus can play number 10, more offensive. The idea is to use the characteristics of the players in the first eleven.” Kudus missed Ghana’s 2026 World Cup campaign through injury and is expected to return to international duty later this month when the Black Stars face Côte d’Ivoire and The Gambia in the AFCON 2027 qualifiers. However, his involvement will now depend on whether he can regain full fitness before Carlos Queiroz names his squad.

Houthis say Saudi Arabia hits Yemen with 54 strikes after attack on bases
items.description: Yemen’s Houthis said on Monday Saudi Arabia launched airstrikes across the west of the country after the Iran-backed group earlier announced it targeted military bases in the kingdom. The group, fighting the Saudi-backed, internationally recognised government, last week seized control of Yemen’s Red Sea coast and the Bab al-Mandab Strait, which has become vital as the wider US-Iran war chokes the Strait of Hormuz. The Houthis said Riyadh targeted Yemen with 54 strikes over 24 hours, after the group fired dozens of drones and missiles at Saudi military facilities, prompting the Saudi civil defence to issue alerts in the southern cities of Khamis Mushait and Abha. The civil defence later issued a brief alert for Najran in southwestern Saudi Arabia without elaborating on the cause for the warning. A Khamis Mushait resident told AFP he heard “intense blasts” which left fires burning for a “long time”. “Honestly, we couldn’t sleep at all.” Houthi missile attacks in western Yemen killed eight troops from Yemeni government forces, two military sources with the Aden-based administration told AFP. The Iran-backed group’s Al-Masirah TV channel said two civilians were killed in Saudi strikes that destroyed a bridge in Taiz province, which has seen some of Yemen’s fiercest clashes in recent days. The renewed fighting in Yemen comes as the wider regional war remains at a stalemate. But US President Donald Trump on Monday said he was open to holding talks with Iran. “The failing Nation of Iran wants to make a deal, quickly and badly. I will determine whether or not the U.S.A. will choose to engage — The concept of which we are open to,” Trump said on his Truth Social network. – Wider regional war – On Monday, a proposed meeting between Gulf states and Iran over the future of Hormuz was postponed, with Tehran accusing Riyadh of using Yemen as a “pretext” to delay the talks. Tehran has long supported the Houthis, a member of its anti-Israel “axis of resistance”, including with weapons and technology, but analysts dispute the extent to which Iran is behind the renewed fighting. “Iran does not interfere in Yemeni affairs,” foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei told reporters on Monday, saying the Houthis are “entirely independent actors who make their decisions based on their own interests”. Saudi Arabia’s de facto ruler Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman was expected to hold talks with Egypt’s President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi on Tuesday, Cairo announced. Mirette Mabrouk, an expert with the Washington-based Middle East Institute, said Prince Mohammed would seek “assurances that if necessary, Egypt will step up to protect Bab al-Mandab”. She said Egypt, whose vital Suez Canal route has also been threatened by the Houthi blockade, “will fight if necessary, but that is not the default position”. “The default position is to exercise every other option before that,” she added. Last week, US media reported Trump had rejected a personal request from the Saudi crown prince to intervene in the war. Yemen’s prolonged civil war had been dormant for four years before reigniting in July over an Iranian flight to the capital Sanaa, becoming the latest conflict drawn into the wider regional war. The Houthis’ military spokesman Yahya Saree on Monday said Saudi Arabia “conducted 54 airstrikes over the past 24 hours using F15 and Typhoon aircraft”. He said the areas of Taiz, Lahj, Al-Jawf, Marib, and Hodeida were targeted. – Forced to flee – Yemeni government forces on Sunday said they had recaptured positions in the southwestern province of Taiz from Houthi fighters and carried out airstrikes, telling the official Saba news agency they killed at least 10 gunmen. The Saudi crown prince received US Central Command chief Admiral Brad Cooper in Jeddah on Monday to discuss “the latest developments in the region”, according to Saudi news agency SPA. The US admiral travelled to Saudi Arabia on Thursday for urgent coordination meetings, according to US news site Axios. The Houthis seized Yemen’s capital Sanaa in 2014 at the outset of the civil war, driving the government to Aden in the south. The following year, Saudi Arabia led a coalition to intervene on the side of the government, launching wave after wave of airstrikes as the conflict escalated into one of the worst humanitarian disasters in the world. items.title: Ghana’s reputation must not be dented by self-centred individuals – Madina MP on cocaine seizure
items.description: The Member of Parliament for Madina, Dr Francis-Xavier Sosu, says Ghana’s international reputation must not be damaged by the actions of individuals seeking to enrich themselves illegally. His comments follow the reported seizure by French customs authorities of nearly 3.9 tonnes of cocaine, valued at about €225 million, from a container of plastic waste that arrived at the port of Dunkirk from Ghana. The Madina MP has called for a thorough investigation into the shipment and urged the authorities to bring anyone found culpable to book. He said President John Mahama and the NDC government had worked to position Ghana as a respected global player in diplomacy. He also commended the Foreign Affairs Minister, Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, for his efforts to project Ghana as a country of integrity and a leader in democracy in Africa. According to Dr Sosu, Ghana’s reputation is a national asset that must be protected through transparency, accountability, and strict enforcement of the law. He said that the actions of a few individuals must not be allowed to undermine the country’s hard-earned standing in the international community.

items.title: MTN Ghana pushes digital growth for SMEs as sixth business clinic ends in Accra
items.description: MTN Ghana has reaffirmed its commitment to accelerating the growth of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) through digital transformation, access to finance and market expansion, as it concluded its sixth SME Business Clinic for the year in the Greater Accra Region. The two-day clinic, held under the theme of developing effective marketing strategies for domestic and global business advantage, brought together over 200 entrepreneurs from diverse sectors to equip them with practical tools, knowledge and partnerships needed to move their businesses from survival to sustainable growth. Addressing participants, Senior Manager for SME Sales, Business Broadband and Partnerships at MTN Ghana, Mr. Mohammed Abubakar Sadic, said the programme was designed to close critical gaps limiting the potential of Ghanaian SMEs. “We are gathered here today as part of MTN Ghana’s Small and Medium-sized Business Clinic for the Greater Accra Region to develop an effective marketing strategy for domestic and global business advantage. The programme has brought participants to be equipped with the tools, knowledge and opportunities they need to grow,” he said. According to him, MTN Ghana has developed a suite of digital solutions tailored to address everyday SME challenges. One flagship solution is Yellow Biz, which provides reliable internet connectivity and enables businesses to create professional websites through WebWiz, giving them visibility beyond Ghana. “We also provide Microsoft 365, which includes productivity tools such as Microsoft Teams. These solutions enable business owners and employees to communicate and collaborate effectively from different locations,” Mr. Sadic explained. He said another critical intervention is Business Eye, a simple CCTV surveillance system that allows entrepreneurs to monitor their shops and offices remotely. “Many entrepreneurs are reluctant to leave their businesses because they are concerned about security and accountability. Business Eye enables them to see what is happening at their premises wherever they are. The system has different power options, including electricity and solar energy, and users can store their recordings securely in the cloud,” he noted. The solution, he said, gives business owners peace of mind to attend training programmes, meetings and other engagements while remaining connected to their operations. Recognizing the dominance of women in Ghana’s SME sector, MTN has introduced Adwumapa, a package specifically designed for women entrepreneurs. “Statistics show that women lead more than 51 per cent of SMEs in Ghana, and MTN is committed to supporting their growth. Adwumapa provides affordable voice and data services, as well as important benefits such as Doctor on Call. We recognise that many women working in our markets may not have enough time to visit health facilities for routine medical consultations. Doctor on Call gives them access to qualified medical professionals,” he said. The package also includes insurance protection, while SME Plus offers similar affordable voice, data and communication benefits for the broader SME community. Both packages include unified communication services that allow businesses to operate a dedicated telephone number through their internet connection. Mr. Sadic said these interventions have become necessary because MTN’s research has identified significant gaps in digital adoption among Ghanaian businesses. “Many SMEs are doing impressive work, but their failure to adopt digital tools is slowing their progress. For businesses to grow exponentially, they must embrace digital transformation and integrate these tools into their operations,” he stressed. Beyond technology, he identified access to financing as another major constraint. To address this, MTN is partnering with financial institutions through its SME Accelerate initiative. “Through our SME Accelerate initiative, MTN is partnering with financial institutions to help entrepreneurs obtain loans. MTN Mobile Money also provides loan services to them with flexible repayment terms. When customers borrow and repay successfully, they improve their chances of accessing additional credit to expand their businesses,” he said. At the Greater Accra clinic, Fidelity Bank participated in educating entrepreneurs on financing opportunities. Eligible SMEs can access short-term loans through MTN Mobile Money, while businesses requiring larger facilities can be referred to partner banks. The clinic also serves as a networking and market access platform. Through initiatives like Y’ello Biz and market activations, participating businesses are supported to reach new customers locally and globally. “We have successfully concluded our sixth SME Business Clinic, and the response has been fantastic. He added that MTN is working with its partners to monitor participating businesses after the programme to assess impact. So far this year, MTN has held clinics in the Volta, Eastern, Ashanti, Western, Northern and Greater Accra Regions. In the Northern Region alone, participants travelled from Tamale, Bolgatanga, Wa and parts of the Savannah Region. In total, more than 1,400 SMEs have been trained this year, building on four clinics held last year. To deepen impact, selected entrepreneurs with strong business potential will be enrolled in a 13-week mini-MBA programme organized in partnership with a business school. This year, about 90 operators will benefit, with MTN Ghana covering the full cost. They will be placed into cohorts, mentored, and certified upon completion. Participants in the clinic received certificates of participation, while outstanding businesses will be recognized at the SME Ghana Awards next month. Mr. Sadic said MTN’s strong belief in the SME sector stems from its strategic role in Ghana’s socio-economic development. “Mes contribute significantly to the country’s Gross Domestic Product and provide a substantial proportion of employment opportunities. When SMEs are properly equipped and supported to grow, Ghana’s economy also grows. Lead Consultant for the 2026 Accra SME Business Clinic, Mr. Richard Maglo, urged SMEs to build marketing strategies that are research-based and capable of competing both locally and globally. Mr. Maglo said marketing has evolved from the production, sales, and marketing eras into the relationship and social eras, where technology informs business decisions. “Marketing has evolved, and it’s more scientific. The decisions we take must be research-based. You must research to understand the market need, so that when you are producing, the needs of the market become the blueprint upon which products and services are delivered,” he explained. He noted that many SMEs in Ghana were established on the wrong foundation, producing goods first before looking for buyers, instead of identifying market needs to drive production.” A lot of SMEs have been established with the wrong foundation. They have produced something and are now looking for who will buy it. But actually, you must look for the need of the market, and that should drive what you are producing,” he said. While SMEs already employ about 70 to 80 percent of Ghana’s population and contribute significantly to GDP, addressing these structural shortfalls would help businesses expand, increase profit margins, and last longer. “My advice is that for SMEs to be very relevant in today’s market space, they must let research inform their decisions, not their feelings and not their intuition,” he added. CEO and Founder of Pins and Scissors Limited, Ms. Letitia Ohene Asiedu, described the workshop as educational, insightful, and beyond expectations. “When you are running a business, you need somebody who really understands the market to coach you, and in Ghana, we lack that. This program taught us how to have a long-term plan and market our businesses internationally,” she said. She applauded MTN for focusing on entrepreneurs, noting that tailored business packages and data support open doors for growth. Ms. Asiedu, who participated for the first time after missing previous regional editions, praised the resource person for using practical, relatable business examples. She said she learned how to position her brand against competitors, improve packaging and branding, and build lasting customer relationships through consistent follow-ups. I have already started applying it.

items.title: Tanger : l’ONCF ouvre la course aux travaux du futur RER
items.description: Le projet de liaison ferroviaire entre la gare de Tanger Ville et l’aéroport Ibn Battouta, via le Grand Stade, franchit un nouveau jalon. L’Office national des chemins de fer (ONCF) vient d’engager une procédure internationale de présélection en vue de la réalisation des travaux d’infrastructure et de génie civil de cette ligne, appelée à constituer la première composante du futur réseau de transport express régional (RER) de Tanger. Le projet passe ainsi à une phase plus opérationnelle. À travers son pôle dédié aux projets de lignes à grande vitesse, l’ONCF a lancé un appel d’offres avec présélection portant sur les travaux liés à cette nouvelle liaison. Le marché est réparti en trois lots principaux, en fonction des caractéristiques des différents tronçons, des territoires traversés et des contraintes techniques liées à l’insertion d’une nouvelle infrastructure ferroviaire dans des espaces déjà structurés par des axes de transport et soumis à une forte expansion urbaine et périurbaine. Longue d’environ 22,5 kilomètres, la future ligne sera aménagée en double voie électrifiée. Elle doit assurer une liaison directe entre le centre de Tanger et l’aéroport Ibn Battouta, tout en desservant plusieurs pôles résidentiels et économiques ainsi que des équipements majeurs. Son tracé traversera successivement les territoires de Tanger Ville, Beni Makada, Aouama et Gzenaya. L’ouverture de la procédure de présélection intervient après une phase consacrée aux études et à la conception technique. L’étude préliminaire a permis de définir les différentes composantes du tracé, les ouvrages nécessaires, les points de raccordement ainsi que les stations et points d’arrêt appelés à assurer la desserte des secteurs traversés. Le futur axe doit ainsi proposer une desserte ferroviaire à plusieurs points stratégiques. Depuis la gare de Tanger Ville, appelée à constituer le terminus du RER, la ligne desservira notamment des stations urbaines intermédiaires à Mghogha, Aouama et El Bharayine, avant d’atteindre une station dédiée au Grand Stade Ibn Battouta. Le tracé se poursuivra ensuite vers la station des Facultés, puis jusqu’au terminus associé au nouveau bâtiment de l’aéroport Tanger Ibn Battouta. Le projet permettra ainsi de créer une liaison ferroviaire directe entre le centre urbain et la plateforme aéroportuaire. Il desservira également plusieurs équipements structurants de la ville, notamment le marché de gros et la nouvelle gare routière. À travers cette infrastructure, le projet vise à faciliter les déplacements au sein de l’agglomération tangéroise et à améliorer les connexions entre ses différents quartiers et principaux équipements. L’enjeu est d’autant plus important que l’extension du tissu urbain accroît les besoins en transport collectif capables d’absorber les flux de voyageurs, tout en améliorant l’accès ferroviaire à l’aéroport et au Grand Stade. Trois lots et un ouvrage de près de 6 kilomètres L’ONCF a réparti les travaux d’infrastructure et de génie civil en trois lots, présentant des caractéristiques différentes en matière de longueur et de nature des ouvrages à réaliser. Le premier lot concerne le tronçon reliant la gare de Tanger Ville au point kilométrique 11+500, sur une longueur d’environ dix kilomètres. Cette partie présente une contrainte technique particulière en raison de son insertion dans un environnement ferroviaire existant et en exploitation. Les travaux devront notamment permettre la création d’une plateforme destinée à une voie unique, en parallèle des emprises ferroviaires actuellement utilisées, dont la ligne Tanger-Fès et les infrastructures dédiées au transport des voyageurs. La réalisation de ce tronçon devra ainsi être articulée avec la circulation des trains et les infrastructures déjà en service, afin de permettre l’intégration de la nouvelle liaison dans un environnement ferroviaire actif. Le deuxième lot s’étend sur environ 7,5 kilomètres, entre le point kilométrique 10+800 et le Grand Stade Ibn Battouta, situé au PK 18+300. Il prévoit la réalisation d’une plateforme ferroviaire complète à double voie, destinée notamment à assurer la desserte de la zone du stade et son raccordement au reste de la ligne. Le troisième lot constitue l’un des volets les plus complexes du projet sur le plan de l’ingénierie. Il reliera le Grand Stade à l’aéroport Tanger Ibn Battouta sur une distance d’environ six kilomètres, jusqu’au nouveau bâtiment de l’aéroport, au PK 24+250. La conception retenue pour ce tronçon repose principalement sur la réalisation d’un ouvrage ferroviaire surélevé continu d’une longueur proche de 6.000 mètres. Cette infrastructure permettra à la ligne de franchir les principaux axes routiers et voies de circulation rencontrés sur son parcours, tout en s’insérant dans le tissu périurbain en expansion entre le Grand Stade et l’aéroport. L’objectif est également de limiter son impact sur la circulation routière et les infrastructures existantes. The post Tanger : l’ONCF ouvre la course aux travaux du futur RER appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Black Maidens confident of WAFU B title defense ahead of Burkina Faso clash
items.description: Ghana’s U-17 female national team, the Black Maidens, are confident ahead of their WAFU Zone B U-17 Girls Cup opener against Burkina Faso on Tuesday. The Black Maidens, who will represent Ghana at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco next month, are also using the tournament in Côte d’Ivoire as part of their preparations for the global competition. Head coach Joe Nana Adarkwa says the team is determined to successfully defend the title they won last year after beating Nigeria’s Flamingos in a thrilling final at the Ghanaman Soccer Centre of Excellence in Prampram. Adarkwa says the primary objective is to use the tournament to assess his players and fine-tune the squad ahead of the World Cup. “We are here to compete for the World Cup. We are going to use this tournament to assess our players, prepare them and go into the World Cup, and hopefully that will give us a good result.” Despite the focus on preparation, the coach insists the Black Maidens are in Yamoussoukro to compete and defend their title. “We are here for business. We are here to compete and compete with the best teams like Nigeria and all the other teams here.” Adarkwa also stressed the importance of having a well-balanced squad, saying every department has been strengthened to ensure Ghana can compete at the highest level. “If you want to compete with the best, you have to strengthen your team.” The Black Maidens will also draw confidence from their status as defending champions, with Adarkwa believing last year’s triumph has lifted the team’s spirit ahead of the tournament. “Everything is high because we are defending champions. The last one that we played in Ghana, we won it, so the spirit is already high. We are here to defend it.”

items.title: Transformation numérique : Cybastion annonce un investissement de 300 millions de dollars au Sénégal
items.description: Le Sénégal franchit une nouvelle étape dans sa stratégie de transformation numérique. À Washington, l’entreprise américaine Cybastion a annoncé un investissement de 300 millions de dollars destiné à accompagner le développement de l’écosystème numérique sénégalais . Cette annonce intervient dans le cadre de la dynamique engagée par les autorités sénégalaises pour renforcer les infrastructures, les services et la souveraineté numériques du pays. Cette enveloppe constitue un signal important pour le développement du secteur numérique, considéré comme l’un des leviers de la transformation économique et administrative du Sénégal. Elle intervient alors que le pays cherche à accélérer la mise en œuvre de ses ambitions dans le domaine du numérique, en cohérence avec l’Agenda national de transformation Sénégal 2050 et le Masterplan 2025-2034. Un investissement stratégique L’annonce de Cybastion intervient dans un contexte marqué par la volonté du Sénégal de renforcer ses capacités technologiques et de réduire sa dépendance à l’égard des infrastructures numériques extérieures. Le développement d’infrastructures adaptées doit notamment permettre de mieux sécuriser les données, d’améliorer les services numériques et de favoriser l’émergence d’un écosystème technologique national. À travers cet investissement, Cybastion entend ainsi participer à la consolidation des bases technologiques nécessaires à la transformation numérique du Sénégal. L’entreprise américaine est déjà présente sur le continent africain, notamment dans des projets liés aux infrastructures numériques et à la cybersécurité. La souveraineté numérique en ligne de mire Au-delà du montant annoncé, l’enjeu est également celui de la souveraineté numérique. Pour le Sénégal, la maîtrise des infrastructures, des données et des technologies constitue désormais un élément stratégique de la transformation de l’État et de l’économie. Cette orientation rejoint les priorités affichées dans le cadre de Sénégal 2050, qui fait de la transformation structurelle de l’économie et du développement des capacités nationales des axes majeurs de l’action publique. La Présidence met d’ailleurs en avant la Stratégie numérique du Sénégal parmi les documents de référence de cette politique. Un potentiel pour l’économie numérique L’arrivée de nouveaux investissements dans le secteur pourrait également contribuer à stimuler l’activité des entreprises technologiques sénégalaises, à développer les compétences et à créer de nouvelles opportunités pour les jeunes et les professionnels du numérique. Le Sénégal dispose déjà d’un écosystème technologique dynamique, avec des entreprises, des start-up et des acteurs publics engagés dans la digitalisation des services. L’enjeu sera désormais de transformer les annonces d’investissements en infrastructures opérationnelles, en emplois, en compétences et en services numériques accessibles aux citoyens et aux entreprises. Avec les 300 millions de dollars annoncés par Cybastion, Dakar entend ainsi renforcer son positionnement dans le paysage numérique africain et accélérer la concrétisation de ses ambitions en matière de souveraineté et de transformation digitale.À mon avis, pour un article du Soleil, le premier titre est le plus équilibré : il met immédiatement en avant le secteur, le montant et le Sénégal, sans surcharger le titre. C.G. DIOP

items.title: Cancers pédiatriques: le combat pour l’identification des signes d’alerte et la détection précoce des tumeurs infantiles
items.description: Détecter les cancers pédiatriques précocement et agir vite. Tel est l’objectif principal poursuivi par l’Ong Action femme et enfant contre le cancer (Afec). À cet effet, elle a réuni, le samedi 12 septembre 2026, des acteurs communautaires et des journalistes en santé. À cette occasion, des spécialistes ont invité à une vigilance accrue et à une orientation rapide des enfants malades vers les centres de soins. Surtout dans un contexte marqué par des pesanteurs socioculturelles, un manque de ressources et des difficultés à référer les patients à temps. Les tabous continuent d’entourer les cancers, souvent associés à la mort, à la peur, au fatalisme et au silence. Ainsi, le diagnostic est souvent tardif, ce qui réduit considérablement les chances de guérison. La situation n’est pas meilleure chez les enfants, dans la mesure où nombreux sont ceux qui ont encore du mal à admettre que ces derniers peuvent être touchés par le cancer. Consciente de ce défi, l’Ong Action femme et enfant contre le cancer (Afec) initie des activités de sensibilisation et de renforcement des capacités. Dans le cadre de « Septembre en or », mois dédié au cancer des enfants, tout comme « Octobre rose » l’est pour les cancers féminins et « Novembre bleu » pour ceux affectant les hommes, la session du samedi 12 septembre 2026 a réuni des acteurs communautaires et des journalistes spécialisés en santé. Pour Diarra Guèye Kébé, présidente de l’Ong Afec, l’édition de cette année s’inscrit dans le cadre de leur « Plan stratégique 2026-2030, qui place la détection précoce et le plaidoyer institutionnel au cœur » de leurs actions. Cela d’autant plus qu’en raison de certaines croyances socioculturelles, des parents banalisent les signes d’alerte, différant ainsi les consultations dans les structures de soins. Aucun moyen de prévention n’étant disponible, encore moins un vaccin, la seule possibilité reste la vigilance concernant les signes visibles. « La grande difficulté est qu’on n’a pas de moyen de prévention. Il n’y a pas non plus de vaccin pour prévenir les cancers, il n’y a pas d’imagerie qui puisse les détecter. On doit donc sensibiliser les familles et la population aux signes visibles. On doit aussi former les acteurs de première ligne, les médecins généralistes, les spécialistes pour qu’ils reconnaissent ces cancers très tôt et qu’ils envoient l’enfant dès les premiers signes vers les centres de soins, parce que le temps est un facteur de pronostic majeur dans la prise en charge des cancers pédiatriques », souligne le Dr Fatou Binetou Diagne Akondé, oncologue-pédiatre. Ce faisant, elle insiste sur la sensibilisation des populations et l’orientation des acteurs communautaires. La pharmacienne et gestionnaire de projet, Fatou Lama Dièye, ajoute : « Le diagnostic tardif est un obstacle à une prise en charge optimale dans des contextes à ressources limitées. » Pour gagner du temps et faire en sorte que l’enfant arrive tôt dans les structures sanitaires, elle insiste sur ce qu’elle appelle les « 3 R » : reconnaître, référer et rassurer. Cependant, elle attire l’attention sur les limites relevées dans le circuit de référencement de l’enfant malade, notamment le manque de moyens des parents, le manque de coordination entre les professionnels de santé et les erreurs pouvant retarder le diagnostic. Le Dr Mame Ndella Diouf, qui a évoqué le diagnostic précoce des leucémies (le cancer le plus fréquent chez l’enfant au Sénégal), estime que le faible taux de guérison qui se situe à moins de 20 % en Afrique contre 95 % dans les pays riches est imputable au retard de diagnostic, au manque de moyens diagnostics ainsi qu’à l’indisponibilité des médicaments. De son côté, le Dr Raïhanatou Diallo, ophtalmologue ayant abordé le rétinoblastome (un cancer qui affecte les yeux), préconise de démarrer le processus de prise en charge dès les postes de santé. « Il faut référer à temps, dès la suspicion de la maladie », indique-t-elle. Toutefois, elle précise qu’il n’est pas nécessaire pour les agents de santé de première ligne (les infirmiers, par exemple) de faire des investigations qui risquent de retarder la prise en charge. En outre, le Dr Ndèye Fatou Sow, oncologue-pédiatre ayant traité des tumeurs cérébrales et du lymphome de Hodgkin (cancer des ganglions lymphatiques), estime que les familles doivent être écoutées, surtout les mères. Selon elle, ces dernières doivent être attentives à tout changement survenant chez l’enfant afin de solliciter à temps les structures de prise en charge. Rappelant que le cancer pédiatrique n’est pas une fatalité, Diarra Guèye Kébé, la présidente de l’Ong Afec, estime « qu’aucun enfant ne devrait être privé de la chance de guérir par manque d’information ». Maïmouna GUÈYE

items.title: Nigerian and Canadian Gambling Industries Compared
items.description: Nigeria and Canada are among the world’s most active gambling markets, but they have developed in very different economic and regulatory environments. Both are experiencing rapid digital growth , rising mobile participation and increasing pressure to protect consumers, yet their dominant products, payment systems and levels of regulatory maturity differ considerably. Two Large but Unequal Markets Canada’s gambling industry generated an estimated C$15.6 billion in revenue during 2025. Around 60% of Canadians report spending money on gambling in a typical month, while the country is estimated to have more than 19 million active online gamblers. Nigeria’s market is harder to measure because substantial activity takes place through unlicensed or informally regulated channels. Industry estimates place total Nigerian gross gaming revenue at approximately US$3.6 billion in 2025, with sports betting contributing around 70% to 75%. Estimates of active Nigerian players range from 50 million to 60 million, while daily wagers may exceed ₦10 billion. These numbers cannot be compared directly because Nigerian and Canadian reports frequently use different definitions of wagers, revenue, accounts and players. Nevertheless, they demonstrate that both countries possess large, increasingly digital gambling audiences. Digital Competition and Casino Bonuses Online operators in both markets compete through mobile applications, broad game catalogues, faster payments and promotional incentives. With so many providers competing, Casino Guru review the best offered welcome bonuses in Canada, helping users compare promotions alongside conditions such as wagering requirements, expiry periods and game restrictions. Promotions are particularly visible in competitive online markets. However, a large headline bonus does not necessarily represent greater value. Withdrawal limits, minimum deposits and wagering conditions can significantly reduce its practical benefit. Canada’s most developed competitive model is Ontario. During the 2024/25 fiscal year, Ontario’s regulated private iGaming market processed C$82.7 billion in wagers and generated C$2.9 billion in gaming revenue. Both figures increased by more than 30% year on year. Casino games led the market, ahead of sports betting and peer-to-peer poker. Nigeria’s online sector is more heavily centred on football betting. European competitions, particularly England’s Premier League, generate substantial activity . Low minimum stakes, widespread smartphone use and agent-based deposit networks have helped betting reach consumers across different income groups. Similar Regulatory Structures A major similarity is decentralisation. Gambling in Canada is principally managed by provinces, while Nigeria moved decisively towards state-level control following a Supreme Court judgment on 22 November 2024. The Nigerian ruling found that lottery and gaming regulation belongs to the states rather than the federal government , except in the Federal Capital Territory. Operators may consequently need multiple state licences, creating additional compliance costs and uncertainty for businesses serving customers nationwide. Canadian provinces also follow different approaches. Ontario permits licensed private online operators, while provinces including British Columbia and Quebec primarily rely on government-controlled platforms. Alberta has also pursued legislation supporting a competitive regulated online market. Canada’s framework is generally more established, with clearer reporting standards, mature lottery corporations and stronger enforcement. Nigeria’s state-based regime is still evolving, particularly for online services that cross internal borders. Different Product Preferences Product mix is one of the clearest differences. Nigerian gambling is dominated by sports betting, especially football. Virtual sports, lotteries and casino games are also available, but fixed-odds betting remains the industry’s central commercial product. Canada has a more diversified market encompassing lotteries, land-based casinos, electronic gaming machines, online casino games, sports betting, bingo and horse racing. In Ontario’s regulated online market, casino products have commonly represented more than 80% of wagers, whereas betting has generally accounted for a much smaller share. Land-based gaming is also more economically significant in Canada. Nigeria has physical casinos and betting shops, but mobile betting and neighbourhood agents are more important to mass-market participation . Payments, Technology and Accessibility Smartphones are central to both industries. Canadian customers benefit from high internet penetration, widespread card use and established banking infrastructure. Nigerian operators have adapted to a mobile-first population by integrating bank transfers, fintech wallets, USSD services and cash-based agent networks. Nigeria’s younger population offers significant long-term growth potential. Canada, meanwhile, benefits from greater average purchasing power and more developed digital infrastructure. Nigerian customers may place smaller individual bets, but high participation and frequent wagering can produce considerable aggregate volumes. Consumer Protection Challenges Both countries face concerns around problem gambling, advertising exposure, underage participation and offshore operators. Canada generally provides more formal self-exclusion programmes, deposit controls and provincial support services. Ontario is also developing centralised self-exclusion across regulated operators. Nigeria’s fragmented framework can make consistent age verification, advertising supervision and player protection more difficult. Unlicensed activity remains a major concern, with some estimates suggesting that more than half of Nigerian online gambling revenue may still sit outside the regulated market. Outlook Canada is moving towards broader regulated competition while retaining provincial control. Nigeria offers faster demographic and mobile-led growth but faces greater regulatory fragmentation and enforcement challenges. Both markets are likely to expand digitally. Their long-term success, however, will depend not only on wagers and revenue, but also on whether regulation can keep pace with technology, promotions and cross-border operators while providing meaningful protection for players. The post Nigerian and Canadian Gambling Industries Compared appeared first on Vanguard News .

Mehdi Halaoui, Directeur général de l'Office national du tourisme tunisien. items.title: 5 players who deserve a Black Stars call-up for AFCON 2027 qualifiers
items.description: With the Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers approaching, Black Stars head coach Carlos Queiroz will have some difficult decisions to make when selecting his squad. While several established players remain automatic choices, along with some players who missed the World Cup through injury, a number of Ghanaians abroad are making strong cases for an opportunity to be selected for the AFCON qualifiers. Here are five players who deserve consideration for a Black Stars call-up. Augustine Boakye Augustine Boakye has made an impressive start to the 2026/27 campaign with Saint-Étienne. The versatile attacker has recorded three goals and two assists in five Ligue 2 appearances, playing 377 minutes. His pace, creativity and versatility make him a strong option for the Black Stars. Boakye was also part of Ghana’s 2026 World Cup squad but is yet to make his senior international debut. Rahim Ibrahim Rahim Ibrahim has quietly established himself as an important midfielder for Slovan Bratislava. The 25-year-old has made four appearances and two starts this season, scoring twice in 151 minutes. He has also gained valuable European experience and made his UEFA Champions League debut for Slovan against Paris Saint-Germain. With Thomas Partey currently unavailable, Ibrahim could provide an additional option in midfield and potentially fill the void left by the Black Stars vice-captain. Joseph Opoku At just 20, Joseph Opoku is making his mark in English football following his move to Swansea City. The winger impressed at Zulte Waregem last season, recording three goals and seven assists in 26 appearances as the club secured promotion. He has continued that form in the Championship, scoring twice in six appearances and playing 343 minutes. His pace and attacking ability could provide Ghana with another option on the wings. Nathaniel Adjei Nathaniel Adjei could provide valuable depth at centre-back. The 24-year-old has made two Ligue 1 appearances for Lorient this season, playing 270 minutes. He has won seven aerial duels and recorded four tackles, while boasting an 87% duel-win rate. His physicality and defensive qualities make him worthy of consideration for the Black Stars. Prince Osei-Owusu Prince Osei-Owusu’s goalscoring form makes him particularly difficult to overlook. The 29-year-old striker has scored 13 goals and provided six assists in 22 MLS appearances this season, playing 1,792 minutes. At 1.91m, his physical presence and aerial ability would also give Ghana a different option in attack. In a nutshell, Ghana have plenty of attacking talent, but current form should be an important factor in AFCON selection. Augustine Boakye offers creativity, Rahim Ibrahim provides midfield depth, Joseph Opoku brings youthful attacking quality, Nathaniel Adjei strengthens the defensive options, while Prince Osei-Owusu’s goalscoring record makes him a compelling choice. All five deserve to be in the conversation for a place in Ghana’s AFCON squad. The Black Stars will begin their 2027 AFCON qualifying campaign away to Côte d’Ivoire in Bouaké on September 24, before hosting The Gambia at the Accra Sports Stadium on September 29. The two fixtures will mark the beginning of Ghana’s journey to return to the AFCON after missing the 2025 edition in Morocco.

items.title: Bandits kill two inspecting land in Imo
items.description: By Emmanuel Iheaka OWERRI — Two persons have been killed by suspected armed bandits while inspecting a parcel of land in Irete Community, Owerri West Local Government Area of Imo State. A source in the community, who pleaded anonymity, said the victims, accompanied by two others, had gone to inspect the land when the hoodlums allegedly attacked and shot them dead on Monday. One of the deceased was identified as Chigaemezu Ozuzu, a member of a local vigilante group. The source alleged that suspected herders had been terrorising Irete and neighbouring communities, forcing some farmers to abandon their farmlands. “The people went to inspect a land for sale. They were four in number; one of them is a woman. “Two of them escaped and alerted the community. This thing is getting out of hand. They have been terrorising our community and neighbouring communities. We are now scared to go to farm,” the source said. Confirming the incident, the Police Public Relations Officer in the state, DSP Henry Okoye, said the Commissioner of Police, CP Audu Garba Bosso, had ordered the immediate deployment of enhanced security operations to the area. In a statement, Okoye said the deployment followed recent security concerns, including pockets of kidnapping and other criminal activities in Owerri West and Oguta local government areas. He said the operation covers Ejemekuru, Ogbakwu, Izombe, Irete, Umuguma, Okuku, Ndegwu, Amakohia-Ubi and adjoining communities. According to him, the Anti-Kidnapping Unit and Violent Crime Response Unit have been deployed with available operational assets, in collaboration with community vigilantes, to intensify intelligence-led operations and apprehend the perpetrators. “The action follows the attack and killing of two young persons in Irete today, 14 September 2026, by suspected armed bandits. “CP Bosso has condemned the incident and directed the relevant units to intensify efforts to identify and apprehend the perpetrators,” the statement read. The commissioner charged the deployed personnel to remain vigilant, proactive and professional, stressing that the command would not allow criminal elements to establish a foothold in any part of the state. He also directed the operatives to work closely with community vigilantes and other relevant stakeholders. The post Bandits kill two inspecting land in Imo appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: KP CM claims he was 'abducted' by authorities in Lahore; Punjab minister denies allegations
items.description: LAHORE: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Monday claimed he was “abducted” by authorities in Lahore and later “thrown” by the roadside, a claim denied by Punjab Information Minister. “We were abducted, and then, when they received pressure from somewhere, they threw me by the roadside without security and left,” Afridi claimed. Afridi further alleged that there was a “conspiracy to abduct the chief minister of a province”, adding that he had earlier warned that “they want to divide the country”. Speaking to Dawn , a senior KP government official accompanying Afridi said the chief minister had boarded the police van to secure the release of some detained party workers. While some workers were freed, others remained in the van, prompting Afridi to refuse to leave. The police then drove the van a reasonable distance from the spot before removing Afridi from the vehicle, he added. However, Punjab Information Minister Azma Bokhari claimed that the KP chief minister had boarded a police vehicle of his own accord. In the video shared by Bokhari, Afridi can be seen voluntarily walking towards and boarding the police vehicle. He then refuses to dismount, while an individual can be heard asking the chief minister to “please leave the vehicle”. Speaking on Dunya News, Bokhari said that when PTI supporters swarmed the car, the police thought they were being attacked. “There were cameras shooting them, and there was a video from inside the dala,” Azma noted. “The driver thought the vehicle was being attacked, so he drove away, but stopped a short while later and said people got off and sat on the footpath.” Azma claimed that none of the motorists in the area bothered to note that Afridi was sitting on the footpath. Asked if Afridi had been arrested, the minister replied in the negative, citing a lack of police at the scene and the fact that his guards and a cameraman were present. “This is a total drama because people did not come out from Lahore and Punjab,” she added. When asked about Afridi’s claim that he had been released under pressure and left without any security, Azma joked: “The only pressure in that scenario is his low blood pressure.” A post on the KP chief minister’s official X account at around 9pm said Afridi “himself got on a Punjab Police van and reached a police station”. Another post , published minutes earlier, said Afridi was present with party workers at a protest rally on Lahore’s Mall Road. ‘Insult to the mandate’ KP Minister for Information Shafi Jan, in a statement, alleged that Punjab Police had attempted to abduct the KP CM, claiming that he was separated from his security detail and forcibly moved into another vehicle. Jan alleged that Afridi was put into a police vehicle and taken to a remote area, where he was later left without his security detail after “pressure mounted”. He accused the Punjab Chief Maryam Nawaz government of “police high-handedness” and said the treatment of the elected chief minister was unconstitutional and undemocratic. “The attempt to abduct Chief Minister Afridi will be considered an attack on the foundations of the federation,” said Jan. He further alleged that the incident was a “dangerous attempt” to create hatred and confrontation between the two provinces, warning that any attempt to abduct an elected chief minister would be considered an attack on the foundations of the federation. He said the KP chief minister’s “humiliation” would not be tolerated. PTI condemned the “arrest” of Afridi in Punjab, calling it an “insult” to the mandate and dignity of the people of the province. In a statement, the party said the incident, along with recent statements by the Punjab chief minister, risked fuelling “resentment, mistrust and division” among the provinces. PTI said it would not engage in “provincialism, ethnicity, hatred or division”, stressing that the mandate of people across all provinces must be respected. The party urged its supporters to respond peacefully and democratically, saying repression and political victimisation would only deepen public resentment. PTI General Secretary Salman Akram Raja said in a post on X that Afridi’s alleged abduction was an attack on the foundations of the federation and urged the police to “come to their senses”. Afridi’s Lahore visit Afridi turned his Lahore visit into a full-fledged political showdown, lashing out at the Punjab government, refusing security and vowing to rid the country of “fake rulers” through a nationwide street movement on Sept 27. The KP CM changed his detailed Punjab visit plan and travelled directly to Lahore to offer condolences to the bereaved family of senior party worker, who had succumbed to his burn injuries. As the Punjab Police escort created hurdles for party leaders and workers trying to join him, Afridi admonished the policemen, calling them “shameless” and accusing them of pushing a man to his death while he was preparing for Eid-i-Miladun Nabi celebrations. “I do not want security from a force that killed a man preparing for Eid-i-Miladun Nabi,” he said. Responding directly to Punjab CM Maryam, who had said she felt threatened by the other three provinces, Afridi said: “The fake chief minister says she feels threatened not by India but by the other three provinces of Pakistan. I announce today that I feel no threat from my brothers and sisters in Punjab.” The KP chief minister and his cabinet members’ convoy faced police blockades while entering Punjab and later within Lahore, where all entry and exit points had been sealed. As Afridi and his convoy travelled through the city, tensions also ran high between police and PTI workers on several occasions, with reports of scuffles. Earlier, the KP chief minister and his cabinet members received a rousing welcome from party workers at several points along their route. Workers chanted slogans as Afridi addressed them at Do Moriya Pul on Circular Road. Hundreds of party workers lined the city roads, prompting the KP CM to make several stops. He waved to the crowds and raised slogans while standing through the sunroof of his vehicle. The rally, however, caused severe traffic congestion in the Walled City, with frequent stops forcing commuters to use adjoining streets. Railway Station Road and surrounding areas, including Aik Moria Pul, Akbari Market Road, Delhi Gate, Wasanwala Bazaar and Shah Alam Market, witnessed severe traffic jams. Traffic police made unsuccessful attempts to restore the flow. Earlier in the day, police had set up pickets on roads across the city and closed markets around the deceased party worker’s residence, as well as along major roads including Gulberg, Ferozepur Road and The Mall. Following the imposition of Section 144 in Punjab, police attempted to disperse crowds accompanying or welcoming Afridi’s convoy and eventually arrested more than a dozen PTI workers, including PTI Lahore president Mian Akram Usman and vice-president Naeemullah Taj.
